speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) to date, what is the number of self-employed persons (SEPs) who could have qualified for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) but are unable to do so because of their lack of MediSave contributions; and (b) whether the Government will consider providing concessions for SEPs to qualify for WIS by having their MediSave eligibility temporarily lowered in light of the COVID-19 crisis or having their MediSave contributions spaced out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This is because Workfare is a permanent scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The need to meet CPF obligations is part of Workfare's eligibility criteria and is consistently applied to both employees and SEPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This ensures that workers continue to take personal responsibility in saving for their long-term retirement and healthcare needs, while receiving Government support via Workfare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: SEPs are only required to contribute to their MediSave accounts after declaring their incomes at the end of the Work Year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: They have up to two years to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Within the two-year period, SEPs can also choose the mode of payment that best suits their circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We also consider exceptional appeals on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Once the SEP makes the required MediSave contributions in full, they will receive their Workfare payout.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We recognise that this is a difficult period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Taxi and private hire car drivers are also receiving additional financial support from the Land Transport Authority's COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I just wanted to understand if, in fact, SEPs who are unable to make the MediSave shortfall, whether there will be consideration given on a case-by-case basis to defer the time at which they can pay the MediSave or start an instalment plan, but they may still be able to get the Workfare payment before that happens.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I believe the Senior Minister of State did refer to that, but I just wanted to clarify.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The reason I ask this is because I think many SEPs are at the lower end of the income scale and very badly hit by COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: A report by DBS Bank, from December last year, said that those of their customers who are earning less than $3,000 a month, had about one-month of emergency funds left.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This was in December last year, the height of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Just wondering what is the extent of flexibility the Government will show to SEPs in that position?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In fact, these are valid concerns, given the current conditions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I shared in the Ministry of Manpower, we are quite flexible because the SEP has two years to make MediSave contributions and within that, we can provide monthly instalments, or in some cases, as we mentioned, we will put temporary deferment if required.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The difference between the Workfare and CRG, or some of the other assistance schemes, is that, this is more an income top-up supplement as opposed to direct financial assistance that one might get out of SSO or CRG.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, these are slightly different schemes, and therefore, the focus is slightly different too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For most SEPs, the MediSave contribution is far lower than that of normal employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For lower-income workers, I think it goes even lower than that.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To some extent, it is already a low bar and we are giving a long two-year period for SEPs to contribute to MediSave.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think that is generally quite reasonable and certainly, we can give flexibility, where required.
